title: Delineation of areas having elevated electrical conductivity, orientation and characterization of bedrock fractures, and occurrence of groundwater discharge to surface water at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Barite Hill/Nevada Goldfields Superfund site near McCormick, South Carolina
citation: Chapman, M.J., Huffman, B.A., and McSwain, K.B., 2015, Delineation of areas having elevated electrical conductivity, orientation and characterization of bedrock fractures, and occurrence of groundwater discharge to surface water at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Barite Hill/Nevada Goldfields Superfund site near McCormick, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2015-5084, map scale 1:13,300.
notes:
Wells from table 1 (pages 18-19) with table 2 water-quality profile averages (page 25). The lithologic logs of wells BH65, BH66 and BH67 (figures 10-12) were not recorded: the page images show the interval boundaries but the lithology patterns are not rendered, so no interval can be tied to a lithology; the legends were not recorded. The EM-induction depths of high conductivity (about 72 ft in BH33/BH34, about 110 ft in BH51) are geophysical, not geologic surfaces, and were not recorded as surfaces. Regolith thickness 28-57 ft is inferred by the authors from casing depths (page 27); no surface recorded. Water-quality ranges in the abstract and text duplicate table 2 and were not recorded again. pH values have no units printed.
Pages 39-109. Not recorded: (1) the handwritten groundwater-quality profile field forms (pages 69-79, image only; queued for an image re-read) and the OCR of handwritten logging field notes (pages 61-87, garbled); (2) table 3-1 (page 91) tool-rinse quality-assurance samples, whose station numbers are not tied to any location, and the EPA groundwater ranges in that table, which are ranges over several wells; (3) the downhole camera notes of table 2-1 (casing joints, screens, water surface) as well-construction details; (4) pH and specific conductance numbers printed on the figure 27 map, whose pairing with sampling points depends on the layout; (5) FLASH model input and simulated flows (pages 102-107) as model values; (6) surface EM conductivity and penetration-depth estimates as geophysics; (7) general references (software, methods, NC climate, NOAA, rose diagrams). Summary values (page 56) repeat earlier pages. Foliation in IR-1: page 39 gives 222° (N. 42° E.) while pages 13 and 56 give 221° (N. 41° E.). BH51 water level: figure 4-5 (page 96) 45.28 ft vs table 1 (page 19) 46.28 ft.
Image re-read of pp. 69-79 (appendix 1, handwritten field forms; the text layer holds only page headers). Odd pages 69, 71, 73, 75, 77, 78 and 79 are well purge logs used as Hydrolab profiles: per reading the sample time, Hydrolab depth below the measuring point (MP), water temperature, conductivity, pH and dissolved oxygen are water tests (image values). Even pages 70, 72, 74 and 76 are Century tool logs (EM induction/conductivity logging): well name, date, depth of well, water level from MP and the handwritten latitude/longitude are observations. Depths are below the measuring point (MP), not land surface, so no depth_reference is given; the tool logs give each well's MP height above land surface. Doubtful digits are flagged unclear and inferred with the reading noted; struck-out values are not recorded. Not recorded: blank form fields, printed form text (stability criteria, volume factors), tool serial numbers, operators, logging speeds and depth start/end, calculation scribbles in the margins, and the tool-log notes. Conductivity and DO units come from the form's stability-criteria table (inferred).
